title: Rate-aware elasticity controller: target signals, predictive scaling, and safety-curves
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement a rate-aware elasticity controller for Redwood Dedicated that uses a mix of short-term target signals (QPS, p95 latency, token/s per-GPU), workload shape (sequence length distribution, burstiness), and predictive warmup to drive scaling decisions while enforcing strict safety-curves to protect latency SLOs and capacity guarantees. This controller will be pluggable into the existing orchestrator and should support per-tenant throughput targets, global pool constraints, and model-variant fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes scaling decisions at 10s and 60s horizons and exposes the decision reason in tracing
Per-tenant throughput targets (tokens/s) can be configured and enforced with circuit-breaker style fallback to lower-capacity variants
Safety-curves prevent scale-up that could violate GPU warmup or KV cache priming budgets; tests show no more than 5% SLO regressions during synthetic surges
End-to-end integration test with dedicated pool emulation validates cooldown and surge limits (min/max nodes, max_surge 20%, cooldown 120s)
Dashboard shows decision rationale, estimated cost delta, and rollback action for each planned scale event
design_decisions: Primary control loop will be a hybrid PID + predictive model: PID for stable short-term corrections; a light-weight time-series predictor (exponential smoothing + burst classifier) for surge anticipation
Target signals will include QPS, tokens/s, GPU utilization, p95 latency, and active KV cache hit ratio. Token-based signals are primary for LLM throughput guarantees.
Safety-curves are parameterized per GPU family and model bundle: max_tokens_in_flight, warmup_window_sec, kv_cache_fill_threshold. These are stored in the config catalog and versioned.

We will use a two-stage actuation: (1) soft recommendation emitted to orchestrator (dry-run) and (2) enforced action after safety checks pass. This enables canary dry-runs and human review for high-impact changes.
Backoff and cooldown semantics: exponential backoff for repeated failing scale-ups; minimum cooldown 60s for scale-downs and 120s for scale-ups to allow instance warmup and KV cache seeding.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Predictive scaling reduces latency spikes but risks overprovisioning during false-positive burst predictions. We'll cap prediction-driven scale to a configurable fraction (default 30%) of max_delta to limit cost exposure.
Using tokens/s as a primary signal aligns with per-token billing and throughput guarantees but requires accurate token estimation for batched requests; misestimation can cause noisy decisions.
PID-only controllers react slower to abrupt surges; the hybrid approach increases complexity and requires more tuning and observability.
Per-tenant guarantees complicate packing efficiency. We trade some utilization to meet SLAs; future work will explore deficit-sharing and weighted borrowing between tenants.
experiments_and_results: Bench 1 (synthetic bursts): hybrid controller reduced p95 latency spikes by 42% vs baseline reactive step scaler; cost delta +8% in synthetic 10-min bursts
Bench 2 (sequence-length skew): token-aware signal improved scale accuracy for long-sequence workloads; reduced unnecessary scale-ups by 27%

Chaos test (random node loss): controller respected safety-curves and never triggered simultaneous-large-scale-ups that would have violated max_surge; failover fallback to lower-capacity variant worked as expected
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement decision engine library (PID + predictor) and config schema for safety-curves — PR #4213
Phase 2: Integrate with orchestrator API, expose dry-run decisions and tracing — PR #4227
Phase 3: Add per-tenant target plumbing, admin UI for target tuning, and dashboard panels — PR #4251
Phase 4: Run canary in staging with dedicated pool emulator, collect metrics for 2 weeks, iterate on thresholds
Phase 5: Gradual rollout to low-traffic dedicated pools with kill-switch and telemetry alerts
qa_steps: Unit tests for PID and predictor logic with edge-case sequences
Integration test that simulates warmup latency and KV cache priming to validate cooldown windows
Load test with mixed tenants and long-short sequence mixes to verify per-tenant enforcement
Fault injection: drop nodes during predicted surge and verify fallback behaviors
rollback_plan: If we observe >5% SLO regressions or unexpected cost amplification in production within the first 48 hours of rollout, revert orchestrator flag to previous scaler and automatically scale to last known-good capacity. Document incident and freeze controller tuning until root cause is analyzed.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alerts for decision-rate anomalies (sudden repeated scale attempts)
SLO regression alert if p95 latency increases >5% over baseline for 30m
Cost delta alert if predicted weekly cost increase >15% for a pool
Dashboard panel: recent decisions, input signals, prediction score, safety-curve hits
open_questions: Default prediction cap: should we start at 20% or 30% of max_delta?
Tolerance for token estimation error per request — do we need to expose a request-level token estimate confidence metric in the API?
How aggressive should tenant borrowing be during emergencies? automated weighted borrowing or manual operator approval?
